stemMd: Which of the following can most reasonably be inferred from the passage?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The model and age of a used pack are enough to tell a buyer how healthy it is.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Second-life storage is likely to replace the recycling of car batteries altogether before very long.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The cooperative's packs failed early because they had been driven in a hot climate.

options.label: D
options.textMd: A pack that has served a second life yields fewer valuable metals when it is finally sent for recycling.

options.label: E
options.textMd: A fleet's identical packs with charging records suit second life better than a mixed lot.

explanationMd:
Apply the author's conclusion to a new case. The final sentence says second life will survive "where its advantages are greatest, in large batches of identical packs from a single model whose history is known". A fleet's identical packs form a large batch from a single model, and charging records make their history known. A mixed lot has the opposite features, which the third paragraph names as the difficulties: packs from many models that the store must be designed around, and health that cannot be judged without costly testing. So the passage supports preferring the fleet packs.

Argue for each rival before rejecting it. The passage calls second life a step "before they are recycled" and expects it to survive only in some cases, "not as a general answer", so it does not predict the end of recycling. It says two packs "of the same model and age can differ widely in health", so model and age are not enough. It never discusses how much metal a pack yields after a second life. And it gives no climate, hot or cold, for the cooperative's packs.

distractorRationale.b: The passage describes second life as coming "before they are recycled" and says it will survive only in particular cases, "not as a general answer". It never predicts that recycling will be replaced.
distractorRationale.a: The third paragraph says two packs "of the same model and age can differ widely in health", which directly contradicts this choice.
distractorRationale.d: The passage says recycling recovers valuable metals and ends a pack's useful life. It never says that a second life reduces the metals recovered later.
distractorRationale.c: Climate is listed as one factor in a pack's health, but the passage says nothing about where the cooperative's packs were driven or why they failed.

accessibilityText: An inference question about the second-life batteries passage. It asks which statement can most reasonably be inferred. The five choices: The model and age of a used pack are enough to tell a buyer how healthy it is; Second-life storage is likely to replace the recycling of car batteries altogether before very long; The cooperative's packs failed early because they had been driven in a hot climate; A pack that has served a second life yields fewer valuable metals when it is finally sent for recycling; A fleet's identical packs with charging records suit second life better than a mixed lot.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank against an original passage; it tests applying the passage's conclusion to a new case, with distractors that are contradicted or unsupported. Every option is answerable, or refutable, from the passage text alone.

review.author: tolc-i-wave8-verbal-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: The last sentence says second life survives best in 'large batches of identical packs from a single model whose history is known', so a fleet's identical packs with charging records suit it better than a mixed lot. The passage contradicts the claim that model and age are enough (packs of the same model and age differ widely) and the claim that second life will replace recycling (packs get a second life before recycling, and it is 'not a general answer'). It never says why the cooperative's packs failed (no hot climate) and never compares metal yields. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave8-tolci-verbal-run1) reached the same answer: Health depends on how packs were charged, and the last sentence says second life survives in large batches of identical packs from a single model whose history is known, so a fleet's identical packs with charging records suit it better than a mixed lot. Model-and-age-sufficient is contradicted; replacing recycling altogether contradicts 'not as a general answer'; the hot-climate cause of the cooperative's failures and fewer recoverable metals after second life are unsupported.]
